# Character sets: SCS, SI/SO, LS2/LS3, SS2/SS3, DEC Special Graphics.

=== DEC Special Graphics draws boxes
source: vttest menu 3 (character sets); VT100 User Guide table 3-9
input: \e(0lqk\e(Bx
cursor: 1,5
screen:
|┌─┐x......|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== DEC Special Graphics leaves capitals alone
source: VT100 User Guide table 3-9 (only 5/15 to 7/14 change)
input: \e(0ABC
screen:
|ABC.......|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== SO selects G1 and SI returns to G0
source: vttest menu 3; xterm ctlseqs SI, SO
input: \e)0a\x0eq\x0fq
screen:
|a─q.......|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== SS2 shifts one character into G2
source: xterm ctlseqs SS2
input: \e*0\eNqq
screen:
|─q........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== SS3 shifts one character into G3
source: xterm ctlseqs SS3
input: \e+A\eO##
screen:
|£#........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== LS2 locks G2 into GL until SI
source: xterm ctlseqs LS2
input: \e*0\enq\x0fq
screen:
|─q........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== The UK set replaces the number sign
source: xterm ctlseqs SCS (A = United Kingdom)
input: \e(A#
screen:
|£.........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|

=== An unknown set is ignored
source: xterm ctlseqs SCS (unsupported sets leave the designation)
input: \e(0\e(Zq
screen:
|─.........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
|..........|
